name: Service & OS Fingerprinting
description: Ability to identify operating systems, service versions, and application frameworks running on target hosts. Covers banner grabbing, protocol-specific fingerprinting, OS detection techniques, and the use of version detection to inform vulnerability analysis.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to service or OS fingerprinting techniques

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands why identifying service versions and operating systems is important for vulnerability assessment
evidence: Can explain the concept of banner grabbing and version detection
Understands how OS fingerprinting works at a high level (TCP/IP stack differences)
Knows that service versions map to known vulnerabilities

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs basic fingerprinting using standard tools under supervision
evidence: Uses Nmap version detection (-sV) and OS detection (-O) flags
Performs manual banner grabbing with Netcat or Telnet
Correctly interprets version detection output to identify services
Documents fingerprinting results in engagement notes under review

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently performs thorough fingerprinting and uses results to guide vulnerability analysis
evidence: Combines multiple fingerprinting techniques for accurate identification
Uses NSE scripts and protocol-specific probes for detailed enumeration
Correlates identified versions with vulnerability databases (CVE, exploit-db)
Identifies services running on non-standard ports through protocol analysis

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Handles difficult fingerprinting scenarios; develops custom probes; mentors others
evidence: Fingerprints hardened or obfuscated services that evade standard detection
Develops custom Nmap probes or fingerprint signatures
Identifies technologies behind load balancers and WAFs
Mentors junior staff on fingerprinting methodology and interpretation

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines fingerprinting methodology; contributes to tool fingerprint databases; trains teams
evidence: Contributes fingerprint signatures to upstream tools (Nmap, Shodan)
Develops novel fingerprinting techniques for emerging protocols
Authored the lab's service identification methodology
Trains teams on advanced fingerprinting and technology identification

assessment_methods.description: Identify all services, versions, and operating systems on a lab network segment containing both standard and non-standard configurations
Given a host with obfuscated banners and non-standard ports, accurately identify the running services and OS
